Kaziranga National Park · Assam, India

Where elephants, people and roads meet around Kaziranga

Spatial assessment of human–elephant conflict and elephant vulnerability across the park and its 1, 3, 5 and 10 km eco-sensitive rings. Click any map to enlarge it.

Study area

A floodplain park squeezed between a river and a highway

The park lies on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. Its southern edge runs along the NH trunk road, with settlements, cropland and the Karbi Anglong foothills beyond. That road and the river frame every result that follows.

Main map 1 · Conflict

Human–elephant conflict potential

Built from the Human Pressure Index, the Road Exposure map and Elephant Habitat Suitability. Conflict is strongest where good elephant habitat sits next to roads and people.

57.6%
Overall H–E conflict (mean of four rings)
54.9%

60.6%
Conflict, 5–10 km ring
0.65
km of road per km², 0–1 km ring

Human–elephant conflict potential with roads, park boundary and rings.

What the map shows

  • Very high conflict follows the southern highwayA continuous black band runs along the park's southern edge from about 93°08′ to 93°36′ E, widest in the south-west and around the eastern town.
  • Conflict does not fade with distanceIt rises from 54.9% in the first ring to 60.6% in the 5–10 km ring. The outer north and south-west carry large high-conflict patches.
  • The park interior is the calm zoneLow and very low classes fill the central and northern park, where roads are absent and human pressure is low.
  • Roads are densest near the park0.65 km of road per km² in the first ring against 0.32 in the 5–10 km ring. The 3–5 km ring is the second densest at 0.60.
Human Pressure + Road Exposure + Habitat Suitability → Conflict potential

Main map 2 · Vulnerability

Integrated elephant vulnerability

Combines buildings, roads, human pressure, land cover, flood vulnerability and habitat suitability into one score. High vulnerability is a thin band, and it hugs the road.

of that area lies within 3 km

Integrated elephant vulnerability. The legend repeats "Low Vulnerability" for classes 2 and 3 in the source map.

What the map shows

  • A red belt along the southern boundaryHigh vulnerability runs from the south-west lobe near 93°10′ E to the south-east around 93°35′ E, tracking the trunk road and the settlements on it.
  • Hot spots south-west and south-eastLarge clusters sit south of the park near 93°12′–93°18′ E and east of it near 93°33′–93°40′ E.
  • Vulnerability falls with distanceRing by ring, the high + very high share drops from 28.8% to 25.3%, 17.0% and 9.0%.
  • The north-central park is safestVery low and low classes cover the grassland core, away from roads and settlements.
Buildings + Roads + Human pressure + LULC + Flood vulnerability + Habitat suitability → Integrated vulnerability

Main map 3 · Corridors × roads

Elephant corridors and the road network

Six corridors and their migration routes lie on the park's southern and south-western side, the same side as the highway. Each one has to cross the road to reach the hills.

6
Corridors, each with a migration route
6 of 6
Sit on the road side of the park
2
Far-west corridors (Amguri, Deosur)
2
Close south-west corridors (Hatidandi, Kanchanjuri)

Habitat and corridor overlay. Corridors: Kukurakata-Bagser at Amguri, Deosur, Hatidandi, Kanchanjuri, Haldhibari, Panbari.

Road and river network for the same extent. The dark red line is the trunk road.

What the overlay shows

  • Corridors run toward the roadHaldhibari and Panbari leave the park boundary and head south across the trunk road.
  • The south-west cluster is tightestHatidandi and Kanchanjuri start within the 3 km rings, where road density is highest (0.65 km/km²).
  • Far-west routes are longerKukurakata-Bagser at Amguri and Deosur extend well beyond the 5 km ring.
The corridor map has no road layer, so crossings above are read by eye from the two maps. Exact crossing counts need the road and corridor vector files.
Ring figures come from your spreadsheets. In the ESZ workbook, Sheet1 is treated as habitat–flood exposure, Sheet2 as flood vulnerability and Sheet3 as integrated vulnerability. Ring-by-ring values are worked out from the cumulative figures.
